deep.reconstruction:
This folio is mainly the opening of a private letter, not a mathematical text. Top right: a place and date, best read 'Schwerin den 24 September 1858'. The first word matches the 'Schwerin' signature on the next page, not 'Leipzig'. Then comes a salutation to a family member, most likely one of Riemann's sisters, possibly 'Mein liebe Helene!'. Its initial letter has the same Kurrent form as the H of 'Hamburg' in the next line, which argues against 'Ida'. A struck-out false start follows, then the sentence '[Über] Deinen lieben Brief, den ich in Hamburg erhielt, habe ich mich sehr gefreut' ('I was very pleased by your dear letter, which I received in Hamburg'). The letter breaks off there. The next page is a separate formal letter draft in the polite 'Sie' form, also signed 'Schwerin. B. Riemann', so the sheet was reused for drafts.

The mathematical content is minimal and unrelated to the letter.
(1) A small pencil sketch. A horizontal segment runs from a marked point on the left to a vertical line. From there a descending, slightly stepped or oblique line falls to a marked point on a horizontal axis. This is the graph of a function that is constant on an interval and then decreases roughly linearly to zero, a trapezoidal or ramp profile. A cut-off, saturation or discharge curve is one possible reading, but no text tells what it represents.
(2) A single equation, dx/dq = x (the numerator may be another letter, e.g. v). Read as an ODE, its solution is x = C*exp(q), exponential growth. Nothing on the page connects it to the sketch or applies it.
(3) A last line of memo-like words, roughly 'Einfluß[?]. Lehrbücher/Zahlwort[?]. Weber?. Auditorium.' This looks like a to-do or reminder list. 'Weber' presumably means Wilhelm Weber, Riemann's Göttingen colleague and mentor; 'Auditorium' suggests lecture arrangements.

No derivation is carried out, so nothing can be filled in beyond the elementary solution of the ODE, which is mine, not Riemann's.
errors: No mathematical errors: no derivation is present. The relation between the sketch and dx/dq = x is unknown. The sketch shows a piecewise-linear profile, not an exponential, so the two are probably unrelated jottings.
